Ikenna’s Big Kick

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
At just 9 years old, South Africa’s Ikenna Tladi makes history by signing a 7-year deal with AS Roma Academy, becoming one of the country's youngest football exports to Europe.

Unique Selling Point:
Move over, Messi. Make room, Mbappé. South Africa has a new name lighting up the world stage — and he’s only 9.
Ikenna Tladi, a born-and-bred talent from North West, South Africa, has signed a jaw-dropping seven-year deal with Italian giants AS Roma Academy, becoming one of the youngest international recruits in recent history. Now, fresh from a whirlwind signing trip to Rome, he’s back on home soil — and he’s giving us his first-ever TV exclusive.

Summary:
From the dusty grassroots fields of Tshiama Soccer Academy to the floodlights of Old Eds FC, Ikenna’s journey started as soon as he could walk. With a ball never far from his tiny feet and a father — Valentine — who lived and breathed football, the boy’s destiny seemed inevitable.
"I didn’t want to raise just a soccer player," says Valentine. "I wanted to raise someone who could command respect through talent and discipline."
That discipline often turned heads. Valentine’s strict training regimens were misunderstood by many as too harsh. But Ikenna’s rise has silenced every doubter. His viral footwork clips spread like wildfire across YouTube and Instagram, eventually landing on the radar of Roma scouts. By eight years old, he was named Player of the Tournament at an elite European youth showcase while representing AS Roma's U10s. At nine, he wears the Giallorossi badge.

Further information:
Now back in South Africa for a short break, Ikenna will speak on television for the very first time. Until now, he’s only done radio interviews. Cameras will finally capture the charisma, humility, and fierce ambition of the boy who stunned the footballing world.
He’ll speak about:
● Adjusting to life in Italy
● Learning Italian (yes, already!)
● Life inside Roma's prestigious academy
● What it felt like to leave his South African teammates behind — and how they saved the captain’s armband for him.
This is not just about football. It’s about the power of vision, discipline, family, and raw talent. It's about a South African child standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Europe's best. It’s about belief.
Coach Carel Tshiama Mambe, the man who first spotted the spark, says:
“When I saw him touch the ball, I knew. He was born for this.”
And now the world knows too.

Script:


(Ikenna) When I play soccer. I feel like a superhero.

(Xola) Every now and then, a sporting prodigy is discovered.

(Ikenna) They say I'm too young, others say I'm too shy.

(Xola) And, no matter how young or withdrawn the personality, the talent is impossible to ignore.

(Ikenna) I’m not scared of playing with big boys.

(Xola) Ikenna Tladi is such a prodigy… in the most beautiful of games.

(Ikenna) I was born ready!

(Xola) In Houghton, Johannesburg, a group of talented boys chase one dream... stardom. They’re constantly assessed, pushed to earn their place at Tshiama Football Academy. Among them is Ikenna.

(Xola) It feels like SA is at the top of the sporting world right now. We have produced so many talented sports stars. We see them all the time. But this story is different. Ikenna Tladi is just nine years old. And at that tender age, one of the biggest clubs in Italy has come looking for his signature.

(Xola) Like so many kids with big dreams, Ikenna grew up watching the greats.

(Xola) When you watch football, is there any footballer you think you want to play like?

(Ikenna) Messi and Ronaldinho.

(Xola) Because, you play on the wing?

(Ikenna) Yes.

(Xola) and Messi? When he was younger and quicker, he played out wide as well. Did you watch those old games when he was still a winger?

(Ikenna) Yes, when he was like eight years old and nine years old. I used to watch him.

(Xola) What do you think about before you go onto the field?

(Ikenna) I think about God giving me this opportunity to play.
(Xola) And do you get nervous?

(Ikenna) No.

(Xola) Never?

(Ikenna) I never get nervous. I was born ready.

(Xola) I love that!

(Xola) Always close by is his biggest fan: dad, Valentine Uche.

(Xola) When he was one year old, you can see he's got that passion. He wants that round object. That's how I started knowing that, okay, maybe he will play.

(Xola) Ikenna’s mom, Popi also shares a love for and history with soccer. Perhaps it’s no surprise that their son was born with such talent.

(Popi) My dad was a huge Pirates supporter. Used to take me to the stadium sometimes, in Wolmaransstad, you know, that's where I grew up. So I've always loved soccer.

(Xola) And obviously, having met your husband, it was a continuation of that story?

(Popi) It really was. And you know, God works in his own ways, because sports is really what united us.

(Ikenna) By the time Ikenna could walk, the ball was almost always glued to his feet.

(Valentine) Sometimes when you throw the ball to him, like a tennis ball, he wants to grab it with his feet.

(Xola) Valentine trained Ikenna for years.

(Valentine) My idea was to teach him how to be friends with the ball, how to manipulate the ball. If he has that, the rest will come.

(Xola) It took just one match to convince Academy coach, Carol Tshiama Mambe, that Ikenna was special.

(Carel) The boy has a, has a book of skills, you know. Myself, I don't even know. Sometimes I just sit down. I'm like, ''You be the coach”. You know, he's fantastic. His technique, his vision of the game. You know, his love and passion. You know, he wants to win.
(Xola) Impressed by the young player, Coach Tshiama shared videos of Ikenna with his international contacts. Italian Serie A side, AS Roma came calling.

(Xola) Founded in 1927, AS Roma is a top-tier club, home to legends like Francesco Totti and Paulo Dybala, winners of major European titles as recently as 2022. Now they’re Ikenna’s new sporting home.

(Carel) For him, it's special whereby they wanted him.

(Xola) What do you think they saw?

(Carel) Probably it was just his normal but trust me, his 'normal' to a lot of kids is like, it's like something else.

(Xiola) iIt’s literally magic on his shoes, it’s the type of skill that seasoned professionals can only yearn for. He can dribble past defenders twice his age. Or in my case, even more. But it doesn’t just take talent. It takes hours of dedication.

(Xola) Do you remember the day that mom and dad told you about Roma calling?

(Xola) And did you know anything about Roma at the time?

(Ikenna) Yes.

(Xola) You did?

(Ikenna)) I was a big fan of Roma.

(Xola) Really. Did you have a favorite player there?

(Ikenna) Dybala.

(Xola) Wow! Paolo Dybala.

(Xola) And with that, Ikenna was off to Italy, to share training facilities with some of his favourite players.

(Xola) For now, Ikenna travels and lives in Italy with his mother, while his father plans to join them later

(Ikenna) We drive to the academy, and then we train, and then we go home, and then I talk to my dad.

(Xola) Do you miss having all of those sessions that you used to have with dad before you had to go over to Roma?

(Ikenna) I miss them so much.

(Xola) Italy came with a few surprises...like uncut, extra 'crispy' pizza.

(Popi) They just give you a round pizza that looks burnt sometimes but I managed to find the African market and buy some okras there. I make for him but in the beginning it was quite a challenge.

(Xola) When you're in Italy, what do you miss most about South Africa?

(Ikenna) The food, and friends and family.


(Xola) And like, at school, do they speak Italian in class and stuff?


(Ikenna) Yes, sometimes.

(Xola) really?

(ikenna) On Wednesdays, we have English classes.

(Xola) One can imagine there’s a lot of pressure coming from home in order to make sure Ikenna is always at his best. The parents could well be criticised for pushing him a bit too hard but when you spend time with him it’s clear to see there is time given to just be a kid.

(Xola) Okay that’s just a simple pass, I got it. I got it. Oh! You got so lucky! It’s because I gave the ball away.

(Xola) Valentine is unapologetic about his almost militant approach to Ikenna's training, and says the quality of his son’s football is because of the discipline he instilled in him.

(Valentine) For you to get the best out of that child, you need to start it early. Even if you want them to be disciplined, you need to be a disciplinarian.

(Xola) Anyone unfamiliar with Ikenna’s talent was left in no doubt about how gifted he is while watching an international youth tournament last Christmas.

(Xola) While in Joburg, Ikenna joined his old team at the Tshiama Academy for the IberCup.

(Carel) There was a time we were losing. I was stressed. I didn’t know what to do.

(Xola) Down 2-nil, the coach called his secret weapon off the bench.

(Valentine) They kicked the ball. He chest it. He took them step over. He shot - goal!

(Xola) A few minutes later, Ikenna scored the equalizer.


(Carel) And guess what? From there, he carried on and we end up winning the game... the only international cup that we have won so far is the academy, and it was because of him.

(Xola) South African roots, West African flair and a touch of Italy - who knows what jersey he’ll wear? For now, he just wants to play good football.

(Xola) Where do you see him ending up?

(Valentile) The sky is the limit, we don't know, we just pray for the best.

(Xola) Okay that’s just a simple pass, I got it. I got it. Oh! You got so lucky! It’s because I gave the ball away. (Xola) Valentine is unapologetic about his almost militant approach to Ikenna's training, and says the quality of his son’s football is because of the discipline he instilled in him. (Valentine) For you to get the best out of that child, you need to start it early. Even if you want them to be disciplined, you need to be a disciplinarian. (Xola) Anyone unfamiliar with Ikenna’s talent was left in no doubt about how gifted he is while watching an international youth tournament last Christmas. (Xola) While in Joburg, Ikenna joined his old team at the Tshiama Academy for the IberCup. (Carel) There was a time we were losing. I was stressed. I didn’t know what to do. (Xola) Down 2-nil, the coach called his secret weapon off the bench. (Valentine) They kicked the ball. He chest it. He took them step over. He shot - goal! (Xola) A few minutes later, Ikenna scored the equalizer. (Carel) And guess what? From there, he carried on and we end up winning the game... the only international cup that we have won so far is the academy, and it was because of him. (Xola) South African roots, West African flair and a touch of Italy - who knows what jersey he’ll wear? For now, he just wants to play good football. (Xola) Where do you see him ending up? (Valentile) The sky is the limit, we don't know, we just pray for the best.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): At just 9 years old, South Africa’s Ikenna Tladi makes history by signing a 7-year deal with AS Roma Academy, becoming one of the country's youngest football exports to Europe.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Move over, Messi. Make room, Mbappé. South Africa has a new name lighting up the world stage — and he’s only 9. Ikenna Tladi, a born-and-bred talent from North West, South Africa, has signed a jaw-dropping seven-year deal with Italian giants AS Roma Academy, becoming one of the youngest international recruits in recent history. Now, fresh from a whirlwind signing trip to Rome, he’s back on home soil — and he’s giving us his first-ever TV exclusive.
metadata.Summary: From the dusty grassroots fields of Tshiama Soccer Academy to the floodlights of Old Eds FC, Ikenna’s journey started as soon as he could walk. With a ball never far from his tiny feet and a father — Valentine — who lived and breathed football, the boy’s destiny seemed inevitable. "I didn’t want to raise just a soccer player," says Valentine. "I wanted to raise someone who could command respect through talent and discipline." That discipline often turned heads. Valentine’s strict training regimens were misunderstood by many as too harsh. But Ikenna’s rise has silenced every doubter. His viral footwork clips spread like wildfire across YouTube and Instagram, eventually landing on the radar of Roma scouts. By eight years old, he was named Player of the Tournament at an elite European youth showcase while representing AS Roma's U10s. At nine, he wears the Giallorossi badge.
metadata.Further information: Now back in South Africa for a short break, Ikenna will speak on television for the very first time. Until now, he’s only done radio interviews. Cameras will finally capture the charisma, humility, and fierce ambition of the boy who stunned the footballing world. He’ll speak about: ● Adjusting to life in Italy ● Learning Italian (yes, already!) ● Life inside Roma's prestigious academy ● What it felt like to leave his South African teammates behind — and how they saved the captain’s armband for him. This is not just about football. It’s about the power of vision, discipline, family, and raw talent. It's about a South African child standing shoulder-to-shoulder with Europe's best. It’s about belief. Coach Carel Tshiama Mambe, the man who first spotted the spark, says: “When I saw him touch the ball, I knew. He was born for this.” And now the world knows too.
